profileQuestions.label: How many people are in your organization across Asia Pacific?
Which region are you based in?

areas.name: Being seen and heard
areas.blurb: Whether people can see and hear each other clearly, and feel present in the room.

areas.name: Working together
areas.blurb: Whether everyone can contribute, share and be heard, wherever they join from.

areas.name: Spaces and support
areas.blurb: Whether your spaces and support keep up with how people meet now.

scoredQuestions.text: When you join a meeting remotely, how well can you see the people in the room?

options.text: Clearly, and the view follows whoever is speaking
Most people, in one wide shot
Only those closest to the camera
It's hard to make anyone out

scoredQuestions.text: How well can remote participants hear everyone in the room?

options.text: Clearly, even people at the far end
Mostly, with the odd "can you repeat that?"
People often have to repeat themselves

scoredQuestions.text: For people in the room, how present do remote colleagues feel?

options.text: Like they're at the table: large, clear, at eye level
Visible, but small or off to one side
On a laptop or a screen few can see

scoredQuestions.text: When a team brainstorms or uses a whiteboard, can remote participants take part?

options.text: Yes, they add to a shared board in real time
They can see it but can't easily add to it

scoredQuestions.text: How easy is it to start a meeting and share content in your rooms?
Do remote participants get an equal chance to speak?

options.text: Yes, hosts actively bring them in
They're often talked over or forgotten

scoredQuestions.text: Do you have the right spaces for how people meet now?

options.text: A good mix of small and large rooms, all video-ready
Mostly, but small video-ready rooms are always booked
Mainly large boardrooms, few small rooms
Our meeting spaces haven't changed since before hybrid

scoredQuestions.text: How often do people in the office join meetings from their desks instead of a meeting room?
Does anyone own and improve the meeting experience?

options.text: Yes, facilities, IT and HR work together and track how rooms are used
One team owns it, with some data

bands.label: Getting started
bands.headline: You're at [X]%. Your meetings are probably costing your people time and energy.
bands.body: Many workplaces added a camera without rethinking the room. A few focused changes can make a visible difference quickly.

bands.label: Making progress
bands.headline: You're at [X]%. The basics work, but remote colleagues are still missing out.
bands.body: Your teams can meet, but not yet as equals. Your biggest gap below is where you'll see the fastest improvement.

bands.label: Nearly there
bands.headline: You're at [X]%. You're ahead of many, with one or two gaps holding you back.
bands.body: Small fixes in your weakest area can make meetings feel effortless for everyone.

bands.label: Hybrid ready
bands.headline: You're at [X]%. Your meetings are working well for everyone.
bands.body: Keep it that way as your teams and ways of working change.

being_seen_and_heard.headline: Not everyone feels present
being_seen_and_heard.tip: When people can't see or hear clearly, they switch off and stop contributing.
being_seen_and_heard.band4Tip: People can see and hear each other clearly, in the room and remotely.

working_together.headline: Remote colleagues are on the sidelines
working_together.tip: When only the room can contribute, good ideas from remote colleagues get lost.
working_together.band4Tip: Remote colleagues add to the work in real time, not after the fact.

spaces_and_support.headline: Your spaces haven't caught up with how people work
spaces_and_support.tip: When rooms are the wrong size or hard to use, people avoid them.
spaces_and_support.band4Tip: Your rooms fit how people meet now, and someone owns keeping them that way.
